globalContext:
name: CI — Build & Type Safety

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  # MERGE QUEUE (2026-11-11): every required job below also runs on the
  # queued merge-group commit, so a required check is evaluated against the
  # exact tree that will land on main. merge_group carries base_sha and
  # head_sha in place of the pull request pair.
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  # NO push TRIGGER. Removed 2026-09-01 (cost audit).
  #
  # The ruleset is squash-only with required checks, so the merge commit's
  # tree is the PR head tree that every gate already passed. The only job the
  # push event still ran was Post-Deploy Verification, a 2-4 minute CDN poll
  # per merge - 2,653 push runs in August (~8,000 billed minutes) duplicating
  # what post-deploy-e2e.yml (workflow_run on the publisher) and
  # production-integrity-audit.yml already verifies against production. Post-Deploy
  # Verification now runs on the schedules below instead. The daily
  # "is main actually green" schedule remains the whole-branch safety net.
  schedule:
    # The production E2E used to run on every push to main. Club Arena merges
    # about nineteen times an hour, so it installed Playwright browsers and
    # drove a real browser against smarter.poker nineteen times an hour - to
    # test a site that only republishes every seven minutes. Twice an hour
    # tests the same thing.
    - cron: '17 */2 * * *'
    # ── IS MAIN ACTUALLY GREEN? (2026-08-31) ──────────────────────────────
    #
    # Every job below is gated on `github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, so a
    # PUSH to main runs nothing and reports SUCCESS. That is defensible on its
    # own terms - the pull request already tested that tree - but it leaves
    # main itself unverified in two situations that both happen here daily:
    #
    #   1. A squash merge builds a tree that NO pull request ever tested,
    #      whenever main moved between the PR's last CI run and the merge.
    #   2. Anything landed by the GitHub API rather than through a PR.
    #
    # On 2026-08-31 four tests had been failing on main under a green badge.
    # They were found only because an unrelated PR happened to touch tests/,
    # which is the one thing that makes the client suite run. Nothing on main
    # would ever have reported them.
    #
    # Once a day, against main, with no change detection: cheap enough to
    # ignore next to nineteen merges an hour, and the only thing in this file
    # that can answer "is the branch we deploy from actually passing".
    - cron: '35 6 * * *'

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# THE GROUP IS KEYED ON THE HEAD SHA, NOT THE BRANCH — changed 2026-08-26.
#
# It used to be `ci-${{ github.ref }}` with cancel-in-progress, so a new push
# cancelled the run for the previous sha. That is the normal, sensible setup
# and it is also how six pull requests ended up permanently unmergeable:
# #1073, #1083, #1088, #1103, #1117 and #1130 each had CANCELLED as the newest
# ci.yml conclusion on their HEAD sha. A required check that reports
# `cancelled` never reports again on its own. Autopilot cannot merge past it,
# the branch is not conflicted so nothing flags it as stuck, and the pull
# request simply sits there looking fine. All six were re-run by hand today;
# without this change the seventh is only a matter of time.
#
# Keying the group on the head sha means a cancel can only ever remove a
# DUPLICATE run of the very same commit — two events for one sha, which is the
# only case where cancelling was ever safe. A run for the sha the check is
# actually evaluated against can no longer be killed by a newer push.
#
# The current PR event now retires its verified obsolete heads explicitly.
# That bounded step also handles jobs whose always() ignores normal cancellation.
# Historically, a superseded sha's run finished instead of dying early.
# That is a few runner-minutes. The thing it buys is that no pull request can
# be stranded by a check that will never speak again, which cost six of them.
#
# ── AND A DUPLICATE QUEUES, IT NEVER CANCELS (2026-09-26) ──────────────────
#
# `cancel-in-progress: true` on a sha-keyed group was meant to make a second
# event for the same commit cheap. Measured on PR #5242 (head 6a4c6fdc17), it
# did the opposite. Two pushes of that one commit landed in the same second
# (push ids 44577774264 and 44577774629, both before=52a70166e2), so GitHub
# opened two `synchronize` runs: 36154166920 and 36154167205. The newer one
# cancelled the older, and the cancel reached only the four jobs that had not
# started yet - `What changed` among them. Every heavy job below is written to
# FAIL OPEN on `needs.changes.result != 'success'`, so the cancelled run then
# ran the ENTIRE heavy matrix anyway (accounting until 15:50:47), its always()
# gates reported `FIXTURE_GATE_COMPILATION_REQUIRED` in red because compilation
# was `cancelled`, and the surviving run sat pending behind it for 25 minutes
# before starting at 15:51. Push to green: 54 minutes, for one commit.
#
# With `false`, the second run waits and the first finishes untouched: no job
# is cancelled, no gate reads a cancellation, and the first verdict arrives on
# its own schedule. A third event for the same sha replaces the pending one,
# which never started a job. The group key is unchanged, so a newer push still
# cannot kill the run for the sha a required check is evaluated against, and
# superseded heads are still retired by the bounded step in `changes`.
# tests/ci-tells-the-truth-faster.law.test.ts pins both halves.
#
# ── A REPLACED HEAD STOPS AT THE PUSH, NOT 30 MINUTES LATER (2026-10-25) ───
#
# The bounded retire step lives in `changes`, so it only acts once the NEW
# run gets a runner. With the account saturated that was a 25-45 minute
# queue wait, and measured over 300 PR runs (2026-10-23 22:07 to 10-25 03:36
# UTC) 124 runs were superseded while still alive; in a 70-run sample 46% of
# their runner time (2,272 s per run) was spent AFTER a newer push already
# existed - work on a sha nobody can merge, ahead of the publisher in the
# same queue.
#
# ci-supersede.yml joins THIS group for the replaced head (`before` on a
# synchronize, the head on a close) with cancel-in-progress, and runs no job.
# GitHub cancels the old run when the event arrives, without a runner. The
# key here is unchanged, so nothing can ever cancel the run for the current
# head, and the heavy jobs below are `!cancelled()` so that a cancelled run
# actually stops. tests/superseded-ci-stops-at-the-push.law.test.ts.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs.accounting_postgres:
accounting_postgres:
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
       ((github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group') &&
        needs.changes.outputs.head_current != 'false' &&
        (needs.changes.result != 'success' ||
         needs.changes.outputs.server == 'true')))
    name: Accounting transactions (PostgreSQL 17) shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/7
    # Standard GitHub-hosted runners are free for this public repository.
    # Preserve the complete qualification matrix and fail-closed required verdict.
    # Shard 2 builds pinned pg_net against the proven compatible system headers.
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.shard == 2 && 'ubuntu-24.04' || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    # Run 35276340849 reached V31 after 26m13s and exhausted the 30m job cap.
    # V31 passed in 4m31s in 35276304884. Keep room for hosted runtime variance;
    # every case, statement, cleanup deadline and required gate stays unchanged.
    # Run 40528107352 shard 1 reached Spin at 35m52s and hit the 40m
    # job deadline. The comparable successful 40520906517 Spin took 5m23s:
    # 41m15s combined, before artifact cleanup. Fifty minutes retains ~20%
    # hosted variance headroom; all case/statement/cleanup limits are unchanged.
    timeout-minutes: 100
    # ── FOUR SHARDS, EVERY CASE (2026-09-26) ─────────────────────────────────
    #
    # This job was the critical path of every server-touching pull request:
    # 29.5 minutes of one runner executing ~90 steps one after another (job
    # 108270970154: Full weekly accounting 467s, Spin expiry 198s, BBJ 164s,
    # MTT 109s, Diamond SQL 78s, F06 lanes 76s, and seventy smaller suites),
    # while Production Build finished in 3, compilation in 7 and CSS Beat in 18.
    # Queue wait was 2 seconds; the time was all serial execution.
    #
    # Every suite builds its own disposable PostgreSQL 17 cluster, so none
    # depends on another's state. They are split across seven runners by
    # measured weight, each step keeping its own `if:` and evidence upload:
    #   1  BBJ replay, accounting/credit/cash-source suites, Spin expiry
    #   2  Weekly selector and data-console qualification, Diamond SQL
    #   3  F06 custody lanes, tournament probes, Lightning
    #   4  Production alert SQL, cash pg_cron, PKO, MTT, satellite, Breakfast
    #   5  Isolated weekly recompute and its retained evidence
    #   6  Full weekly accounting activation and its retained evidence
    #   7  Certified V31 qualification with its existing phase admission
    # Shards 3 and 4 build the native isolation tester because their suites
    # need it (PG_ISOLATION_TESTER); 1 and 2 do not use it.
    #
    # Nothing is skipped and nothing is weakened: `fail-fast: false` lets
    # every shard finish and report, and the required `Server Engine
    # (typecheck + tests)` aggregate reads `needs.accounting_postgres.result`,
    # which is `success` only when all seven shards succeeded. The normal
    # four-shard baseline took 35m04s; final timings require normal CI evidence.
    # October 12 run 38319524263: shard 1 exhausted its 40m cap; its 25
    # Lightning steps took 692s while shard 3 finished in 878s. Moving only
    # that unchanged family to shard 3 balances observed work (~1570s on 3),
    # preserving the 40m cap, every suite, financial deadline and artifact.
    # October 28 run 40628889736: shard 1 took 2203s, shard 2 827s,
    # shard 3 1462s and shard 4 1198s. The isolated weekly recompute took
    # 766s on shard 1. Move that unchanged proof AND artifact to shard 2:
    # measured workload predicts a ~1593s maximum instead of 2203s,
    # with the same four runners, every assertion and all evidence retained.
    # October 31 run 41200651455: shards 1..4 took 1785/1414/2195/2033s.
    # Move the isolated Diamond group (231s) and backed payout scan (188s)
    # to shard 2, preserving commands, order, artifacts and all four runners.
    # This balances measured work; it is not a promised future duration.
    # November 6 run 42338709472: shards 1..7 took 1530/534/1967/992/728/
    # 683/170s of suite time, so every server pull request waited 34m on
    # shard 3 while shard 7 finished in 3m. The scoped launch reset stays on
    # shard 1: it compiles against the server headers only shard 1's
    # installer provides, and its root npm install is what the later
    # on-time-start step there loads (proved by run 42344546975, where moving
    # it failed both). Moved, unchanged and each with its own evidence step:
    # backed payout discovery,
    # F06 shared hand lanes and atomic departures 3->2; horse settlement-key
    # and adaptive-statistics retention, Midway weekly promo and first-week
    # aggregate 3->5; committed-page and bucket inventory seals, original
    # inventory restoration, downline rake scope, superseded horse actions
    # and the accepted roster 3->6. None uses the isolation tester, pg_net or
    # pg_cron. Predicted maximum ~1530s (shard 1, unchanged) instead of
    # 1967s; shard 3 drops to ~1294s with Lightning whole and the
    # isolation-tester suites kept with their tool.
    # November 7 run 42345829378 then measured shard 1 at 29.4m against 13-20m
    # everywhere else. Root dependencies became common setup (above), and the
    # Spin expiry proof (1->5) and the cashier statement family (1->6, order
    # kept) moved unchanged; none compiles against the server headers, which
    # tests/accounting-shard-prerequisites.law.test.ts now enforces.
    # tests/ci-tells-the-truth-faster.law.test.ts pins the split:
    # every suite step belongs to exactly one shard.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: server/package-lock.json
      - name: Install server test dependencies
        working-directory: server
        run: npm ci
      - name: Install root test dependencies
        # Every accounting shard installs the root lockfile itself, so no
        # suite can depend on another suite's install having run earlier on
        # its shard. Run 42344546975 proved On-time starts silently resolved
        # typescript through the scoped launch reset's own npm ci.
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts
      - name: Install PostgreSQL 17 tools without a default database service
        env:
          PG_CI_SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          pg_ci_build_packages=()
          pg_ci_server_packages=(postgresql-17 postgresql-17-cron)
          pg_ci_fixture_version=
          pg_ci_build_tools_ready=true
          case "$PG_CI_SHARD" in
            1)
              pg_ci_build_packages=(postgresql-server-dev-17 build-essential)
              for pg_ci_tool in cc make; do
                if ! command -v "$pg_ci_tool" >/dev/null; then pg_ci_build_tools_ready=false; fi
              done
              if [[ ! -x /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin/pg_config ||
                    ! -f /usr/include/postgresql/17/server/postgres.h ]]; then pg_ci_build_tools_ready=false; fi
              ;;
            2)
              # The private-record admission proof builds the real pg_net in an
              # isolated private PostgreSQL prefix; never install into the host.
              pg_ci_build_packages=(build-essential bison flex perl bzip2 pkg-config libcurl4-openssl-dev)
              for pg_ci_tool in cc make bison flex perl bzip2 pkg-config curl-config; do
                if ! command -v "$pg_ci_tool" >/dev/null; then pg_ci_build_tools_ready=false; fi
              done
              if ! pkg-config --exists libcurl; then pg_ci_build_tools_ready=false; fi
              ;;
            3|4)
              # The native source/checksum and fixture manifests own this exact minor.
              pg_ci_fixture_version="$(python3 -B scripts/ci/build_pg17_isolationtester.py --print-version)"
              [[ "$pg_ci_fixture_version" =~ ^17\.[0-9]+$ ]]
              pg_ci_server_packages=("postgresql-17=$pg_ci_fixture_version-*" "postgresql-client-17=$pg_ci_fixture_version-*" postgresql-17-cron)
              pg_ci_build_packages=("postgresql-server-dev-17=$pg_ci_fixture_version-*" build-essential bison flex perl bzip2 patch)
              for pg_ci_binary in postgres psql pg_config; do
                pg_ci_actual="$(/usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin/"$pg_ci_binary" --version 2>/dev/null)" || pg_ci_actual=
                case "$pg_ci_actual" in
                  "PostgreSQL $pg_ci_fixture_version"|"PostgreSQL $pg_ci_fixture_version "*|*" (PostgreSQL) $pg_ci_fixture_version"|*" (PostgreSQL) $pg_ci_fixture_version "*) ;;
                  *) pg_ci_build_tools_ready=false ;;
                esac
              done
              for pg_ci_tool in cc make bison flex perl tar bzip2 patch; do
                if ! command -v "$pg_ci_tool" >/dev/null; then pg_ci_build_tools_ready=false; fi
              done
              if [[ ! -x /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin/pg_config ||
                    ! -f /usr/include/postgresql/17/server/postgres.h ]]; then pg_ci_build_tools_ready=false; fi
              if [[ "$PG_CI_SHARD" == 4 ]]; then
                pg_ci_build_packages+=(pkg-config libssl-dev libzstd-dev)
                if ! command -v pkg-config >/dev/null || ! pkg-config --exists libzstd openssl; then
                  pg_ci_build_tools_ready=false
                fi
              fi
              ;;
            5|6|7)
              # Isolated weekly recompute, full weekly activation and V31 use
              # the common PG17 tools; no native compiler or fixture builder.
              # The shared install/readiness check below retains pg_cron,
              # including the full weekly activation fixture on shard 6.
              ;;
            *) echo 'Unknown accounting shard' >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [[ "$pg_ci_build_tools_ready" == true &&
                -x /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin/postgres &&
                -x /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin/initdb &&
                -x /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin/pg_ctl &&
                -x /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin/psql &&
                -x /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin/createdb &&
                -x /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin/pg_dump &&
                -f /usr/share/postgresql/17/extension/pg_cron.control &&
                -f /usr/lib/postgresql/17/lib/pg_cron.so ]]; then exit 0; fi
          # The hosted image also configures Chrome and Microsoft repositories.
          # An unrelated Chrome index hash mismatch blocked this accounting job.
          # Limit this installation to signed Ubuntu and PostgreSQL sources.
          # The same Azure mirror stalled native qualification for 18 minutes.
          # Preserve signed Ubuntu/PGDG sources and every package/test budget.
          # The one shared install (signed Ubuntu/PGDG sources only, the checkout key,
          # bounded retries around every apt call): .github/actions/install-postgres-17.
          PG_UBUNTU_MIRROR=true PG_FIXTURE_VERSION="$pg_ci_fixture_version" PG_PACKAGES="${pg_ci_server_packages[*]} ${pg_ci_build_packages[*]-}" \
            bash .github/actions/install-postgres-17/install.sh
      - name: MTT lobby entries count committed registrations and rebuys
        if: matrix.shard == 4
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
          TMPDIR: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-mtt-lobby-entry-counts.py

      - name: Tournament guarantees include funded bounties
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
          TMPDIR: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-bounty-guarantee-postgres.py

      - name: The finalized-pool freeze refuses what arming it would refuse
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
          TMPDIR: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-finalized-pool-freeze-arming.py

      - name: Cash queues explain their authoritative admission state
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
          TMPDIR: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-cash-queue-feedback-postgres.py

      - name: Cash top-up retries read their original receipt
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
          TMPDIR: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-cash-addon-receipt-postgres.py

      - name: Original committed horse turns have an independent complete census
        if: matrix.shard == 3
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: |
          python3 -B scripts/ci/test-horse-turn-census-packet.py
          node --test tests/operations/horse-turn-census-transport.test.mjs
          python3 -B scripts/ci/test-horse-turn-census-postgres.py --pg-bin "$PG_BIN" --scratch "${{ runner.temp }}"
      - name: Fixed-limit blinds and uncapped buy-ins use the original cash owners
        if: matrix.shard == 3
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-fixed-limit-policy-postgres.py --pg-bin "$PG_BIN" --scratch "${{ runner.temp }}"

      - name: Backup restore aligns standalone sequence owners
        if: matrix.shard == 4
        run: python3 -B scripts/verification-harness/standby-sequence-owners.py --pg-bin /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin --scratch-root "${{ runner.temp }}"

      - name: Runtime privilege changes preserve the schema DDL boundary
        if: matrix.shard == 4
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-runtime-privilege-ddl-guard-postgres.py --pg-bin "$PG_BIN" --scratch-root "${{ runner.temp }}"
      - name: Leaderboard snapshot extrema preserve filtered ranking results
        if: matrix.shard == 4
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-leaderboard-extrema-postgres.py --scratch "${{ runner.temp }}"
      - name: Retention bounds retained prefixes before accounting guards
        if: matrix.shard == 4
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/run_launch_reset_accounting_fixture.py --fixture scripts/ci/fixtures/hand-prune-bounded-scan.sql --candidate supabase/migrations/20261026174211_the_retention_scan_bounds_work_before_evaluating_guards.sql --work-root "${{ runner.temp }}" --pg-bin "$PG_BIN"
      - name: Retention commits one page before releasing maintenance admission
        if: matrix.shard == 4
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/run_launch_reset_accounting_fixture.py --fixture scripts/ci/fixtures/hand-prune-one-page.sql --candidate supabase/migrations/20261029154153_hand_history_pruning_commits_one_raw_page_before_releasing_m.sql --work-root "${{ runner.temp }}" --pg-bin "$PG_BIN"
      - name: Mystery award pages retain every tied reveal exactly once
        if: matrix.shard == 2
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-mystery-award-page-order.py --pg-bin "$PG_BIN" --scratch "${{ runner.temp }}"
      - name: Weekly linked proofs preserve original windows and paid books
        if: matrix.shard == 2
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: |
          python3 -B scripts/ci/test-weekly-linked-window-proof-postgres.py --pg-bin "$PG_BIN" --scratch "${{ runner.temp }}" --output "${{ runner.temp }}/weekly-linked-window-proof.json"
          python3 -B scripts/ci/test-weekly-linked-window-proof-verifier.py --scratch "${{ runner.temp }}"
      - name: Weekly cash boundaries keep original rows and use the frame cover
        if: matrix.shard == 2
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-weekly-pending-funding-index-postgres.py --pg-bin "$PG_BIN" --scratch "${{ runner.temp }}" --candidate supabase/migrations/20261031081522_cover_original_cash_boundary_transaction_frames.sql --output "${{ runner.temp }}/weekly-pending-funding-index.json"
      - name: November 3 zero guarantees preserve separate Horse attendance
        if: matrix.shard == 2
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-nov3-zero-guarantee-postgres.py --pg-bin "$PG_BIN" --scratch "${{ runner.temp }}"
      - name: Retain weekly pending funding index qualification
        if: always() && matrix.shard == 2
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: weekly-pending-funding-index-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/weekly-pending-funding-index.json
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Cash horses use bankroll eligibility and table closure preserves seats
        if: matrix.shard == 2
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/run_launch_reset_accounting_fixture.py --fixture scripts/ci/fixtures/cash-horse-bankroll.sql --candidate supabase/migrations/20261023221116_cash_horses_are_bankroll_only_and_closed_counts_are_truthful.sql --work-root "${{ runner.temp }}" --pg-bin "$PG_BIN"
      - name: The full scheduled horse fleet can play every game
        if: matrix.shard == 2
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/run_launch_reset_accounting_fixture.py --fixture scripts/ci/fixtures/scheduled-horses.sql --candidate supabase/migrations/20261023222825_scheduled_horses_play_every_game_without_roster_restrictions.sql --work-root "${{ runner.temp }}" --pg-bin "$PG_BIN"
      - name: Half cash capacity keeps only measured top performers
        if: matrix.shard == 2
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: python3 -B scripts/qualification/test-cash-half-top-horses.py
      - name: Horse layer drift uses original eligible populations
        if: matrix.shard == 2
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/run_launch_reset_accounting_fixture.py --fixture scripts/ci/fixtures/horse-layer-populations.sql --candidate supabase/migrations/20261025203617_horse_multiboard_descendants_use_their_decision_population.sql --work-root "${{ runner.temp }}" --pg-bin "$PG_BIN"
      - name: Club entry news is shown once across devices
        if: matrix.shard == 2
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
          TMPDIR: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-club-entry-news-postgres.py

      - name: Quick Club Opening Reuses Funded Reserves
        if: matrix.shard == 2
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
          QUICK_CLUB_TEST_WORK: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-quick-club-opening.py

      - name: Digest player periods stay within one daily request
        if: matrix.shard == 2
        env:
          PG_BIN: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
          DIGEST_NATIVE_WORK: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: python3 -B scripts/ci/test-digest-player-period.py

      - name: Digest database sources stay qualified

changes:
    name: What changed
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group')
    # MERGE QUEUE TOKEN CAP (2026-11-11): this job checks out and runs the
    # queued or pull request head's own classifier, so its token is read-only.
    # The one write it used to hold (retiring superseded attempts) lives in
    # retire_superseded below, which runs only main's script.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      head_current: ${{ steps.head.outputs.head_current }}
      phase4: ${{ steps.f.outputs.phase4 }}
      server: ${{ steps.f.outputs.server }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
        with:
          ref: ${{ (github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.event.merge_group.head_sha) }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          # blob:none keeps every one of the 7,223 commits and drops the blobs of old
          # revisions. Measured 2026-09-13, three runs each: 33-35s / 531MB against
          # 36-43s / 766MB, for identical ancestry. Nothing in this repo's workflows
          # reads a historical file version - they ask merge-base, rev-list, log and
          # cat-file -e, which are all commit-graph work - so those blobs were paid
          # for on every run and never read.
          filter: blob:none
          # Classify Git paths without hydrating the full artwork/source tree.
          # Cone mode also retains root package and Playwright configuration files.
          sparse-checkout: |
            scripts
            .github
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: f
        env:
          CI_BASE_SHA: ${{ (github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.merge_group.base_sha) }}
          CI_HEAD_SHA: ${{ (github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.event.merge_group.head_sha) }}
        run: node scripts/ci/classify-ci-changes.mjs
      # ── IS THIS RUN STILL THE ONE THAT WILL BE MERGED? (2026-09-18) ──────
      #
      # The concurrency group above is keyed on the HEAD SHA on purpose, and
      # its comment explains what that bought: a run for the sha a required
      # check is evaluated against can no longer be killed by a newer push, so
      # no pull request can be stranded by a check that will never speak again.
      # Six of them were, before that change.
      #
      # What it costs is that every push to a branch pays for a COMPLETE
      # fan-out, including the ones nobody will ever merge. Measured over
      # 2026-09-17: 309 CI runs across 95 branches, 3.3 full runs per branch,
      # and the five busiest branches alone accounted for 107 of them - 34, 28,
      # 17, 15 and 13 runs, each an agent iterating on the same pull request.
      # The whole account spent 168,011 Actions minutes in eighteen days and
      # stopped dead when it hit its spending limit at 10:11 on 2026-09-18,
      # taking the engine release route down with it.
      #
      # So: keep every FAST gate on every push (they are seconds, they are
      # ungated on purpose, and two of them exist because something reached
      # main unseen), and let the HEAVY matrix - four client shards, four
      # server shards, PostgreSQL accounting, the production build, the CSS
      # beat E2E, the native fixture - run only for a head that is still the
      # pull request's head when its diff is classified.
      #
      # THE MERGE GATE IS UNCHANGED. The final push to a branch is, by
      # definition, its current head, so its run executes everything. Only a
      # sha that has already been replaced skips, and a replaced sha is not the
      # one a required check is evaluated against.
      #
      # FAIL OPEN, always. An unreadable answer means run everything, exactly
      # as `needs.changes.result != 'success'` already means "this diff could
      # break anything". A cost control must never be able to hide a failure.
      - id: head
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CI_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          CI_PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          set -u
          current=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pulls/${CI_PR_NUMBER}" --jq .head.sha 2>/dev/null || echo '')
          if [ -z "$current" ]; then
            echo "could not read the pull request head; running everything"
            echo "head_current=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif [ "$current" = "$CI_HEAD_SHA" ]; then
            echo "this run is the pull request head ($CI_HEAD_SHA)"
            echo "head_current=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "superseded: this run is $CI_HEAD_SHA, the pull request head is now $current"
            echo "head_current=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # Keep always() failure-reporting gates intact. Normal cancellation can
  # leave their old jobs queued; this one event retires only proven older
  # heads of this same PR, never current checks or a production workflow.
  # It holds the only actions:write token in this workflow, so it runs the
  # default branch's script, never code from the pull request or a queue.
